rules.alternateExpression: if detectionRuleDisabled is true, then isDisablingAllowed is true
if detectionRuleDisabled is true and changeTicketExists is false, then isSecurityIncident is true
if reEnablingDisabledRule is true, then isReEnablingAllowed is true
if performedByAutomationAccount is true and changeTicketExists is true, then isSecurityIncident is false
if ruleChangeCompliant is true, then engineerRecorded is true
if ruleChangeCompliant is true, then timePerformedRecorded is true
if ruleChangeCompliant is false, then engineerRecorded is false or timePerformedRecorded is false

variables.name: detectionRuleDisabled
variables.description: True if the detection rule is in a disabled state (has been turned off).

variables.name: changeTicketExists
variables.description: True if a change ticket exists for the change being performed on the detection rule.

variables.name: isDisablingAllowed
variables.description: True if disabling the detection rule is permitted under the policy.

variables.name: isSecurityIncident
variables.description: True if the event constitutes a security incident.

variables.name: performedByAutomationAccount
variables.description: True if the rule change was performed by an automation account (rather than a human engineer).

variables.name: reEnablingDisabledRule
variables.description: True if the action being performed is re-enabling a previously disabled detection rule.

variables.name: isReEnablingAllowed
variables.description: True if re-enabling a disabled detection rule is permitted under the policy.

variables.name: engineerRecorded
variables.description: True if the identity of the engineer who performed the rule change has been recorded.

variables.name: timePerformedRecorded
variables.description: True if the time at which the rule change was performed has been recorded.

variables.name: ruleChangeCompliant
variables.description: True if the rule change complies with the recording requirements of the policy.
